questions.q: When two Before-update Business Rules apply to the same table, what decides which one runs first?
options: Alphabetical order of the rule name
The order field — lower order values run first
They always run at the exact same time, simultaneously
Whichever rule was created most recently
questions.explain: Order is a plain numeric tiebreaker among rules of the same timing on the same table; lower runs first.

questions.q: Given these two Before rules on Incident, which order do they run in?
options: Order has no effect when both rules are Before rules
They run in parallel and the result is unpredictable
Order 100 ('Auto-escalate urgency') runs completely, then order 200 ('Clear urgency') starts
Order 200 always runs first regardless of the number
questions.code:
Before rules on Incident, both update-triggered:
  order 100 — "Auto-escalate urgency for Priority 1"
  order 200 — "Clear urgency when priority is cleared"
questions.explain: Lower order values run first — order 100 finishes in full before order 200 begins.

questions.q: What is the real, overall sequence of a single save operation?
options: Async rules -> Before rules -> database write -> After rules
After rules -> database write -> Before rules -> Display rules
Before rules (in order) -> the database write -> After rules (in order) -> Async rules queued
Display rules -> Before rules -> After rules -> database write
questions.explain: Before rules always complete ahead of the actual write; After rules run once it commits; Async rules are only queued, running later in the background.

questions.q: In this Business Rule script on the base 'task' table, why does the sys_class_name check matter?
options: sys_class_name is required syntax with no functional effect
Without it, the state = 7 logic meant only for Incident would also run for every other table extending task, like Problem and Change
The script would fail to save without that check
It determines which order value the rule is assigned
questions.explain: A Business Rule on a base table like task runs for every extending table unless scoped — the sys_class_name check is what keeps Incident-specific logic from leaking into Problem or Change.

questions.q: Why does a Business Rule defined on the base 'task' table also run for Incident, Problem, and Change Request?
options: Because task is a view, not a real table, so it has no effect on its own
Because those tables extend task, and a rule on a base table runs for every table that extends it unless scoped otherwise
Only if the rule's order field is set to zero
It doesn't — Business Rules only ever run on the exact table they're created on
questions.explain: Table inheritance applies to Business Rules just as it applies to the schema itself — a rule on the parent table reaches every child table by default.
